items.item_text: Medical Assistant Diploma.
To administer injections or provide venipuncture, must have written evidence of validation for training and competence in medication administration by injecting and skin testing.
Experience working in an environment performing tasks related to front and back office duties related to this position.
Experience working in an ambulatory multi-specialty or primary care office.
A minimum of 2 years of Medical Assistant experience.
Prior EMR experience, preferably with EPIC.

Direct Patient Care: Determining the chief complaint and documenting it in the patient's electronic medical record with close attention to accurate use of medical terms. Interviews patient to obtain medical information and record medical history/information, measure vital signs, weight, and height, and records information in the electronic medical record, identifying & addressing outstanding quality measure gaps(exams/procedures per MA protocol). Show patients to examination rooms and prepare them for the physician. Assisting with treatments and exams, provide chaperoning when necessary, including but not limited to new/minor dressing changes; suture removal; staple removal; injections; splints; ace wraps. Explain/demonstrate treatment procedures, medications, diets, or physicians' instructions to patients. Prepare treatment rooms for patient examinations and procedures, keeping the rooms neat and clean and stocked with necessary supplies. Check out: giving patient instructions for discharge, schedule follow up appointments & UCR Health specialty appointments if applicable, identify labs/orders for the patient from their visit, provide any instructions or reminders to the patients for their next visit as directed by the provider(blood pressure/blood sugar logs, etc.). (40% time)

Contact Center: Provides a warm welcome with appropriate etiquette to patients by answering inquiries. Responds to patients in a courteous manner. In the event a patient selects the wrong option, assists patient to the best of their ability to avoid patient dissatisfaction. Comforts patients by anticipating patients' anxieties; answering patients' questions. Following UCRH protocols/workflows - Listens to new symptoms and refers/schedules patient with appropriate level of care, take messages for providers, and assists with inquiries regarding medication refill. Documents conversation/recommendation and routes appropriately in the EMR. (30% time)

Medication Administration and Prescriptions: Prepare and administer medications per policy. In tandem with physician or licensed nurse, authorize drug refills, and provide prescription information to pharmacies. Patient Prior Authorizations: Coordinates prior authorizations and medication delivery between providers and outside pharmacies. Generates authorization for approval from the payor. Researches what pharmacy the patient should go to based on the payor and if any pre-authorization is required. (10% time)

Front Office Support: Reschedules patient appointments at the request of the patient and/or provider. Optimizes patients' satisfaction, provider time, and treatment room utilization by scheduling appointments in person or by telephone. Checks in patients at arrival. Keeps patient appointments on schedule by notifying provider of patient's arrival; reviewing service delivery compared to schedule; reminding provider of service delays; and keeps in regular communication with patients to inform them of delays. Escorts patients to the room where they will meet the provider. Collect copay and patient balances. (5% time)
Other duties as assigned. Participates in administrative and operational tasks related to patient care and clinic needs. (5% time)

Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Maintains patient accounts by obtaining, recording, and updating personal, financial, and compliance information into the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Assists providers and patients with access and navigation to the patient portal. In-Basket Management: Monitor and respond to messages in the EMR in-baskets. (5% time)

Laboratory/Specimen Collection and Processing: Perform routine laboratory point of care testing and sample analyses. Collect specimens, log, and prepare for testing. Retrieves lab and test results as needed and uploads to the medical record. Ensures process is followed for provider review. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Frequently
Write: Frequently
Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Frequently
Reason & Analyze: Occasionally
Bend: Occasionally
Sit: Occasionally
Squat: Occasionally
Stand: Frequently
Walk: Frequently

Other: Must be able to lift up to and push / pull 50 pounds. Must be able to assist patients with mobility during rooming patients and in preparation for exams/procedures. Able to respond to assist in emergency scenarios; administer CPR.
Strong oral and written communication skills to effectively communicate with patients of varying ages and multicultural backgrounds.
Bilingual-English/Spanish.
Must demonstrate customer / patient service skills appropriate to the job.
Ability to maintain a work pace appropriate to the workload.
Must possess the skill, knowledge, and ability essential to the successful performance of assigned duties.
Strong interpersonal skills.
Ability to work well in a constantly changing environment.
Understanding of medical terminology.
Familiarity with universal precautions, handling of bio-hazardous waste, specimen identification and transport.
